canonical_question: What is the mechanical stability of the '19 ± 2.3 GPa' hardness if the grain size increases during service in a 'harsh environment'?

question_variants.question: What is the mechanical stability of the '19 ± 2.3 GPa' hardness if the grain size increases during service in a 'harsh environment'?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper reports a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa for the nanocrystalline film. However, the provided evidence does not contain data or discussion regarding the mechanical stability of this hardness if the grain size increases during service in a harsh environment. The text mentions wear tests at RT and 300 °C but does not link grain growth to hardness degradation in that context.

answers.answer: The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa. The text discusses wear tests at RT and 300 °C but does not provide data on the stability of this hardness value if the grain size increases.
answers.boundary_limitation: No evidence provided on grain growth effects on hardness in harsh environments
evidence_spans: In this work, a refractory high-entropy alloy (RHEA) film of equimolar CuMoTaWV was deposited on silicon and 304 stainless-steel substrates using DC-magnetron sputtering.
A sputtering target was developed by partial sintering of an equimolar powder mixture of Cu, Mo, Ta, W, and V using spark plasma sintering.
The target was used to sputter a nanocrystalline RHEA film with a thickness of ∼900 nm and an average grain size of 18 nm.
